items.stem: Explain why a full turn is 2π radians.
items.answer: The arc for a full turn is the whole circumference 2πr; an angle of 1 radian has arc r, so the full turn is 2πr/r = 2π radians.
items.markingKey: B1 circumference 2πr; B1 divide by r for each radian [2]

items.stem: Explain why the formula s = rθ only works when θ is measured in radians.
items.answer: It comes from s/(2πr) = θ/(2π), i.e. the arc is the same fraction of the circumference as θ is of 2π; that is only true when the full turn is 2π, i.e. radians.
items.markingKey: B1 fraction of circle argument; B1 full turn 2π only in radians [2]

items.answer: Ethan evaluated sin 1.4 in degree mode; with radians the area is ½ × 81 × (1.4 − sin 1.4) = 16.8 cm².
